question: to the Commission Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Sirpa Pietikäinen (PPE) Subject:

The EU directive on the protection of the environment through criminal law1 is an essential tool for combating environmental crimes, which are often linked to organised crime and cause serious damage to biodiversity and significant risks to public health. Although the transposition deadline was 21 May 2026, the majority of Member States have not yet finalised the adoption of the necessary national measures. It is, however, crucial that the implementation of this directive be ambitious and be backed by sufficient human, financial and judicial resources as well as enhanced cooperation between national authorities, European agencies and civil society. In this context, it is essential that the Commission fully exercise its role as the guardian of the Treaties in order to prevent persistent delays, divergences in application and ensure the protection of environmental defenders. 1.
What is the current status of the transposition of this directive in the Member States?
According to what timetable and methodology will the Commission assess the effectiveness of the national measures adopted?
What further initiatives does the Commission intend to take to ensure uniform implementation, in particular with regard to Article 23 on statistical data?
Directive (EU) 2024/1203 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 on the protection of the environment through criminal law (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/1203/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.7.2026) The Commission attaches great importance to the complete and timely transposition of the Directive (EU) 2024/1203 on the protection of the environment through criminal law (’the Directive’) by the Member States. In order to support Member States, the Commission organised three transposition workshops, provided a detailed guidance document and held bilateral meetings with Member States to address specific issues, upon their request. On 21 May 2026, the deadline for Member States to implement the Directive expired. As of June 2026, the Commission received notifications of national transposition measures from nine Member States of which only two indicated a full transposition. The Commission is closely following the transposition process, and will take appropriate steps, as relevant. In accordance with Article 25 of the Directive, the Commission will assess the Member States’ compliance with the Directive by 2028, carry out an evaluation of the impact of the Directive by 2031 and submit the respective reports to the European Parliament and the Council. In accordance with Article 24 of the Directive, the Environmental Crimes Data Committee was set up to establish a standard format for transmitting statistical data to the Commission, as provided under Articles 22-23 of the Directive. Two Committee meetings have already been held, and a third one is foreseen in September 2026.
